newEngineering: One complete owner auth recovery workflow across native MCP browser authorization, separate Google OIDC, passphrase, immutable principal binding, additive Postgres one-use proof, protected preview and rollback. Uses original Google SDK and legacy OAuth issuance, without duplicating registries.
planComparison: Frozen estimate 660 production lines; measured 304 added and 40 removed production lines on exact PR #204 source head, plus 287 lines of new real Postgres and HTTP regression tests. Reusing existing OIDC verification, browser session support, and guarded owner issuance preserved tested behaviors and avoided padding.
relatedWorkDecision: The single P10-7 migration subsection is a coherent account-authority outcome; P10-6 requires explicit separate pilot/public-Google consent/provider acceptance. Merging source is not authorization to enable any runtime flag or retire legacy login.
exceptionEvidence: One full independently eligible roadmap subsection P10-7 with all seven original acceptance criteria mapped and 344 substantive changed production lines spanning owner login, Google callback, API route, SQL schema/transactions, rollback and documentation; not a helper-only PR.

Second original Outcome D subsection P10-6 is genuine external two-user public Google pilot and publication gating. Cannot count an unauthorised provider migration/public activation as progress or invent a second completed subsection merely to satisfy an advisory target.

Real PostgreSQL two-consumer proof, 1951 passing unit tests, original owner/Hub compatibility and full source/RTC/DB CI run #39037581770 justify a high-trust coherent outcome rather than independent smaller security changes.
